newsitem.title: USA: NCAA-UCLA FIRES HEAD BASKETBALL COACH HARRICK.
newsitem.headline: NCAA-UCLA FIRES HEAD BASKETBALL COACH HARRICK.

text.p: Jim Harrick, who guided UCLA to the national collegiate title in 1995, on Wednesday was fired from his post as men's head basketball coach for violations regarding his expense account and recruiting.
"I am announcing today the termination of UCLA men's head basketball coach James R. Harrick," said Chancellor Charles E. Young in a statment issued by the university.
"Coach Harrick has been terminated following a UCLA investigation into an NCAA recruiting violation and subsequent misstatements about the infraction."
Assistant coach Steve Lavin will take over as interim head coach of one of the most storied college basketball programmes in the nation.
The school cited Harrick with violations of both NCAA and UCLA ethics codes.
The 58-year-old Harrick was the second most successful coach in UCLA history behind the legendary John Wooden, compiling a 191-63 record in eight years.

Harrick was named national Coach of the Year in 1995 after leading UCLA to its record 11th NCAA championship and first in two decades. Harrick was the first coach in school history to guide the Bruins to eight straight 20-win seasons.
The Bruins are coming off a 23-8 season that ended with an upset loss to Princeton in the opening round of the 1996 NCAA Tournament.
Harrick came to UCLA in 1988 after serving as head coach at nearby Pepperdine for nine seasons. He had received a five-year contract extension in August, 1995.
UCLA is scheduled to play its first exhibition game on November 12 and open the season by hosting Tulsa November 20.
